memory_candidates.content: When a plan's Phase 1 is a measurement/baseline-reproduction step gated by an explicit Scope Hypothesis with a stated stop condition, run the measurement literally before touching any destructive step -- even when the plan's arithmetic looks internally consistent and well-cited. In this case both a fresh reconversion AND an independently-ingested corpus copy agreed the asserted 4-hit baseline no longer reproduced (measured 2, both known false positives, zero genuine defects): the source PDF outside the repo had apparently already been fixed during the task's own 'supplied evidence' gathering, with no git history or backup marker to record that. Stopping and reporting per the plan's own designed contingency (rather than improvising a workaround) let the requester make an informed call to close the task via reworded documentation instead of a fabricated re-OCR narrative.

Before invoking a codebase's ingest/conversion pipeline to perform a 'mechanical' refresh step, check git status for concurrent uncommitted edits to that pipeline's own scripts -- a sibling task running in the same working tree may be mid-refactor. Invoking mid-edit tooling is not a deterministic 'mechanical' step even if the end goal (swap in fresh content) is simple, and combined with the target content already passing every check, the safer choice was to measure with the gate's own check functions directly (imported, not invoked via the changing scripts) and record a reasoned exclusion rather than force the swap.
